text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"By default the kubelet sends HTTP/2 requests for HTTP probes.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 explicitly says the default is HTTP/1.1, not HTTP/2.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"By default the `kubelet` sends HTTP/1.1 requests when executing an HTTP probe."}]},{"claim_text":"Using HTTP/1.1 instead requires the H2CContainerProbe feature gate.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 says HTTP/1.1 is the default, and the H2CContainerProbe gate is required for HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c), not for HTTP/1.1.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"By default the `kubelet` sends HTTP/1.1 requests when executing an HTTP probe."},{"index":0,"quote":"This requires the `H2CContainerProbe` [feature gate](/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/feature-gates/) to be enabled on both the `kube-apiserver` and the `kubelet`."}]},{"claim_text":"A TCP probe considers the container healthy if it can open a socket on the given port.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 states the kubelet attempts to open a socket on the specified port and considers the container healthy if it can establish a connection.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"With this configuration, the kubelet will attempt to open a socket to your container on the specified port. If it can establish a connection, the container is considered healthy"}]},{"claim_text":"If the readiness probe fails, the kubelet restarts the container.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 2 says a failed readiness probe marks the pod unready and stops traffic;
